summary: The off-centre turntable recommendation hard-codes a 450 cm belt half length and reports Y centre+450, but CFG belt half_len is 380.
failure_scenario: Edit CFG turntable cy so the turntable centre check fails (more than 10 cm from mid-wheelbase) and rerun fit_check.py. The generated Recommendations section then says 'with a 450 cm half length the belt then reaches about Y <y+450>', which is 70 cm longer than the 380 cm half length build_env.py actually builds (belt end y+380, drums and plates further).
evidence: Read tools/fit_check.py:1058-1059 against tools/build_env.py:98 (half_len 380) and the comment at build_env.py:96. Failure-path text only, reached only when the 'Turntable centred' check is not PASS; the current committed report takes the PASS path. Not executed (needs pxr and the external blueprint).

summary: Method and limits: a numpy re-implementation of the mesh_compute.py kernels (profile, loft_faces, rings, sweep_rings, resample, corners) was injected as the mesh_compute module so tools/meshlib.py and tools/build_env.py build_parts()/nozzle_mesh()/collector_mesh() ran on CPU without Warp, CUDA or pxr. No GPU, renderer, codec, install or download was used. Native Warp kernel behaviour itself is not established by this; the stand-in only reproduces the kernel source arithmetic.

Stand-in fidelity: all 45 meshes built by build_parts() have face counts, vertex counts, faceVertexCounts and faceVertexIndices identical to the committed models/wind_tunnel/assets/test_section.usda, and point positions agree to 6e-5 cm (float32 rounding). The committed asset is therefore not stale against the builder and CFG, and the stand-in matches the real Warp output for these inputs.

Winding: every closed connected component of every environment mesh (690 components, including chamfered boxes, discs, tubes, sweeps, hex bolt heads and seam bands) has positive signed volume (outward). No same-direction duplicate directed edges (consistent winding) in any mesh. The only open edges are the intended ones: nozzle and collector shells at their ends and floor feet, the unbottomed annulus bands under the floor, and single-polygon honeycomb and screen backing.

Degenerate geometry: no zero-area faces, repeated vertex ids, zero-length face edges, coincident points within a mesh, unused points or non-finite coordinates in any of the 45 meshes. Chamfer clamp (0.45 of the smallest half extent) and profile radius clamp are never hit by the supported CFG; no duplicate-vertex case from radius equal to half width arises.

Authored data in the committed asset: for all 45 meshes the faceVarying normal and st index arrays have one entry per face corner, every normal is unit length and none opposes its face winding (0 corners); the committed present.usda Dolly (216) and Orbit360 (361) camera matrices match build_present dolly_pose/orbit_pose to 4e-13 in eye and aim, at times k*2.5.

Axes and dimensions: nozzle lip apex y 762.5 and collector lip apex y -1100 give the documented 332.5 cm and 450 cm Y gaps to the domain; flange, bolts, ribs, seams, supports and portal columns sit on the intended skin offsets; the portal columns and header clear the settling chamber box by 4 cm; screen backing profile equals the collector inner profile at its station; RectLight rotations send emission to -Y, +Y and -Y as commented (the comment that local Y maps to world +Z is really -Z, harmless for a centred rectangle). No environment mesh AABB overlaps the flow domain except Floor items with top at or below 0.30 cm.

Reference and payload wiring: blueprint_override.usda sublayer path ../../../external/blueprint/source/specializations/auto-aero/stages/Main.usda resolves from models/wind_tunnel/scenes to the repo-root external clone path fit_check.py uses; payload ../assets/test_section.usda with explicit </Environment> and an explicit list-op matches the asset default prim and CLAUDE.md contract; present.usda and present_payload.usda differ only in the arc keyword and doc string. The external blueprint is absent, so composition itself was not run.

fit_check numerics: point_tri_dist matched a dense-sampling brute force on 300 random triangles (worst error 0.019 against a sampling resolution of the same order) and handles collinear and point triangles; classify_point on the stand-in nozzle and collector meshes gives opening (2,2,2) inside the duct, material (1,1,1) in the skin and air outside, as the report assumes.

Presentation checks: check_dolly closest approach recomputed on the stand-in meshes plus the Ahmed box is 45.0 cm (Dolly) and 80.7 cm (Orbit360) to TestFloor, consistent with the documented 44.9 cm; half the largest step is 7.5 and 8.6 cm, consistent with the loop bound. Static Hero camera keeps the 4.3x Ahmed box in frame (NDC within +-1); Detail and Wake intentionally do not frame it and are not checked for it. Stilt plates clear the centre belt plates by about 2.35 cm, just over the 2.0 cm margin.

Texture and UV plumbing: parameter order in tex_perf, tex_honeycomb, tex_floor and tex_belt matches the _material kernel indices; perf (10 rows) and honeycomb (4 by 7 periods) tiles are integer multiples of their lattice so repeats are seamless; seeds do not collide between materials; resample() semantics (cell-centred, spacing within 1 percent of pitch for the bolt paths) match the expectation in check_compute.py. Kernels were not run.

Already-reported candidates were not re-reported (RollingRoadFrame lookup, vertex-only jet clearance, post-save NaN guard). Not verified: any behaviour that needs the blueprint clone (camera samples, car LFS content, composition), pxr authoring through usdex, the USD validator, and rendering.
